title: Hymn 1, sound: jai ghar keerat
hook: jai ghar keerat aakheeai kartey kaa hoe beechaaro (Gauri Deepaki M1, ang 12)

segments.voice: Yesterday, Sohila, the night song: five hymns that close the day. Did you read or hear it before bed? Today we open the first of the five, and we start with its sound. Day four hundred twenty-two.

Every house has a sound. The kettle in the morning. A television murmuring in the next room. Somebody's music through a closed door, the same three songs on repeat. If a stranger stood in your hallway for an hour with their eyes shut, they would know a lot about who lives there. The first hymn of Sohila begins with exactly that idea. It doesn't describe a temple, or a mountain, or a holy city. It describes a house, any house, and asks what you would hear if you stood inside it. Today: the opening line, sound first.
screen: `EVERY HOUSE HAS A SOUND.` → `WHAT WOULD A STRANGER HEAR?` → `HYMN 1 BEGINS IN A HOUSE.`

segments.voice: Here it is, slowly: jai ghar keerat aakheeai, kartey kaa hoe beechaaro. It's by Guru Nanak, in Raag Gauri Deepaki, on Ang 12 of the Guru Granth Sahib. Take it word by word. Jai ghar: in the house where. Keerat: praise. Aakheeai: is spoken. Kartey kaa: of the Creator. Hoe beechaaro: and there is reflection, real thought about the One. So: in the house where the Creator's praise is spoken and reflected on. The next line finishes the thought: in that house, sing Sohila, and remember the One who made you. Notice the pairing. Not only praise, but praise and reflection together. Words that are said, and words that are thought about. Then comes the refrain, the line the whole hymn keeps returning to. In paraphrase: sing the song of praise of my Fearless One; I would give myself for that song, which brings lasting peace. Fearless is nirbhau, the same word you met in the Mool Mantar at the very start of the path. Here is the quiet surprise in the first line. Ghar can mean a building, but in Gurbani it also points inward: the heart, the body, a gathering of people. So jai ghar is a house with a door and a kettle, and it is also you. Many Sikhs hear it both ways. The house where praise is sung might be a gurdwara, a kitchen, or the inside of one tired person at eleven at night. The Guru doesn't say which house. He says what kind.
screen: `JAI GHAR: IN THE HOUSE WHERE.` · `PRAISE SPOKEN, PRAISE REFLECTED ON.` · `THE REFRAIN: MY FEARLESS ONE.` · `GHAR: A BUILDING, AND A HEART.` · then, large: `JAI GHAR KEERAT.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: say the first line aloud. Jai ghar keerat aakheeai, kartey kaa hoe beechaaro. Say it once just for the sound, letting the syllables come slowly. Then say it again and listen to the room you're in while you say it. What else does this house sound like right now? A fridge, traffic, a dog? Let the line sit among those sounds. Then be quiet and breathe, and let the room go on sounding. If you pray, you can whisper the line once more at the end. The bell holds the time.
Hymn 1. The first of Sohila's five, by Guru Nanak: in the house where the Creator's praise is spoken and reflected on, in that house, sing.

Your line: jai ghar keerat. In the house where praise is sung. Tonight, before bed, notice what your home sounds like in its last hour, and let one good word be part of it. Day four hundred twenty-two.

howItsDone: Sikhs recite Kirtan Sohila at night before sleep, beginning with this hymn of Guru Nanak; in gurdwaras it is sung when the Guru Granth Sahib is closed and laid to rest for the night.

myth: the first hymn of Sohila begins by describing a temple
it begins with a house, any house where the Creator's praise is spoken and reflected on.
ghar in Gurbani can point to the heart as well as a building
many Sikhs hear jai ghar as a home and as the person inside it.
the refrain calls the One fearless, nirbhau
the same word that appears in the Mool Mantar.

fork.setup: the hymn says what makes a house the right place to sing Sohila. what is it?
options: a house that has been specially consecrated.
a house where the Creator's praise is spoken and reflected on.
a house with a copy of the scripture in it.
fork.reveal: the line asks only for praise and reflection together. it names no kind of building at all.

original.note: Gurmukhi: keerat, praise; the word at the center of Sohila's first line.

trapdoor: what you thought: jai ghar keerat is the name of a place.
what it means: in the house where praise is spoken, and where people reflect on the Creator, sing Sohila.
what a scholar hears: the hymn is in Raag Gauri Deepaki, opens Kirtan Sohila on Ang 12, and pairs keerat (praise) with beechaar (reflection).

sources.ref: Gauri Deepaki M1, Ang 12 (Kirtan Sohila, hymn 1)
